keyTerms.definition: Moving one course mechanism into an unfamiliar setting.
Transfer, not recognition.

recall.question: What does each transfer set do?
recall.answer: Moves one course mechanism into an unfamiliar setting.

sections.title: T1: a flow with a uniform base

keyTerms.definition: Uniform(0,2pi); log-density -1.8379 inside, undefined outside.
What breaks first; invertibility untouched.
Addition mod 2pi with a periodic base; the minimal fix.

recall.question: T1 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: what breaks first (base log-density, support, or invertibility), and the base log-density at 1.0. Q2: a concrete input leaving the support, and what the evaluator returns. Q3: the minimal fix keeping exact likelihood, and what you lose.

sections.title: T2: a GAN for medical rows with a privacy bar

keyTerms.definition: No synthetic row may match a real row on all three fields.
The GAN: its loss is not a density, cannot certify absence of copying.
Min distance from each synthetic row to the real set; the test instead.

recall.question: T2 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: which concept blocks certification from the loss, and what test instead. Q2: two readings of 100% discriminator accuracy and which kills the project. Q3: the new privacy failure a VAE introduces.

sections.title: T3: diffusion on a phone with 4 steps

keyTerms.definition: eta=0 on strided timesteps; the first sampler to reach for.
1-step student: gain real-time, lose diversity and exact inversion.

recall.question: T3 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: the sampler to reach for first and its assumption. Q2: the washed-out mechanism in one sentence and the cheapest no-retraining fix. Q3: what distillation gains, loses, and the deciding experiment.

keyTerms.definition: Per-token: B's 64 tokens per 3 bases vs A's 4 per base; incomparable.
(NLL in nats / ln 2) / bases; the deciding metric.

recall.question: T4 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: is lower-perplexity B better, with the deciding arithmetic. Q2: convert both to bits per base with the formula. Q3: what changes in the cost model for byte-level at L=8192.

sections.title: T5: posterior collapse in a new domain

keyTerms.definition: KL 0.0003/dim, sharp reconstructions; the decoder ignores z.
Both fixes move up the curve: more rate, less distortion.

recall.question: T5 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: diagnose in one sentence. Q2: explain the sharp-reconstruction vs garbage-prior asymmetry. Q3: two fixes (objective + architecture) and how each changes the rate-distortion tradeoff.

sections.title: T6: score model on bounded sensor data

keyTerms.definition: The score blows up near 0 and 100; smoothing turns the edge into a slope.
sigma_min: the hidden free parameter that can flip ODE-likelihood rankings.

recall.question: T6 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: what happens to the learned score near the bounds, with the mechanism. Q2: the hidden free parameter in the ODE likelihoods and how it flips rankings. Q3: the minimal preprocessing and what it costs.

keyTerms.definition: Needs a metric; token IDs are categorical, so the slope is meaningless.
Conceptually awkward: derived for the data space, not an embedding proxy.

recall.question: T7 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: what Lipschitz means on discrete token IDs and why the penalty is awkward. Q2: what distribution the interpolations come from and why the penalty may not bind. Q3: one non-adversarial alternative from the course.

sections.title: T8: anomaly detection under a latency SLA

keyTerms.definition: MAF: 1 parallel pass; AR transformer: 1 forward pass; both parallel for scoring.
The likelihood averages over points; a missing fraud shape barely moves the mean.

recall.question: T8 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: each model's scoring direction and per-point serial cost at D=128. Q2: the arithmetic picking the SLA winner. Q3: the evaluation concept explaining the missed fraud shape and the test to add.

sections.title: T9: memorization audit for a face diffusion model

keyTerms.definition: Independent sampling; 3 near-duplicates at 0.5 px reject it.
At low noise the score points at training points; the sampler walks back.

recall.question: T9 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: the null hypothesis in one sentence. Q2: attack 'diffusion cannot memorize' with one mechanism. Q3: the pre-signing audit design (samples, reference, rule).

sections.title: T10: the vendor s FID win

keyTerms.definition: Matching feature moments with the wrong shape: same FID, garbage images.
Precision/recall, held-out likelihood or NN screen, MMD; win 2 of 3.

recall.question: T10 asks three questions. Name them.
recall.answer: Q1: the cheapest counterexample keeping their FID 8.2. Q2: the two omitted pieces a fair comparison needs. Q3: the one-week no-raters evaluation suite with 3+ metrics and the rule.
